title: How An Infinite Hotel Ran Out Of Room
beats: You are the manager of a hotel with infinitely many rooms; claim that even this can run out of room
All rooms full, one new guest: shift everyone down one room
A bus of 100 guests: shift everyone down 100
Infinite bus: pause to think, then double room numbers to free all odd rooms
Infinitely many infinite buses; the spreadsheet with bus rows and seat columns gives each person an ID
Zigzag line through the grid, then straighten into a line: grid becomes list, so everyone fits
Party bus with seatless passengers named by infinite strings of A and B; Abba introduced
Abba objects: infinite people, infinite rooms, why not fit?
Assign rooms to names on a list, then show the diagonal flip that builds a missing name
Name differs from every listed name by one letter on the diagonal; rooms are countably infinite, bus uncountably
Some infinities are bigger; led to your device; story for another time

theory: The hotel is a toy world where one operation, relabelling rooms, is reused at ever larger scale until it finally fails. The failure is staged through a character who raises the learner's own objection, so the diagonal argument is received as an answer.
velocity: Scene builder: reusable relabelling animation (shift, double, zigzag) whose same visual vocabulary repeats across scales
Orchestrator: playbook 'ladder until break': escalate the same problem until the trick fails, then introduce the new idea
Learner model: pause at the infinite bus beat (1:04) and ask the learner to predict before revealing
Ghost hands: draw the diagonal flip live, one letter at a time, to make it checkable
quote: What do you mean? There's an infinite number of us
